source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio campus holds 36 MW, the fourth-largest disclosed data center capacity in Texas, representing 7.6 percent of the state's 475 MW across 19 published facilities.

The facility's technical footprint of 296,000 square feet and compliance certifications for healthcare, government, and payment processing indicate a campus designed for conventional enterprise and cloud workloads before AI accelerator density became the dominant driver of data center demand. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the 36 MW capacity translates to roughly 900 racks, though the operator publishes no tenant mix or current utilization. This capacity ceiling may reflect either the campus power delivery infrastructure or IT equipment limits, since no grid connection or backup generation details are disclosed.

Texas ranks second nationally in published data center capacity, yet this campus is one of only 19 facilities statewide with disclosed specs among 133 mapped locations. Most Texas data centers do not publish capacity, making it impossible to assess whether power, cooling, or real estate is the binding constraint on AI scaling in the state. The facility's suitability for AI depends on whether its power delivery systems and physical layout can support accelerator-dense clusters, which the published data does not establish.
